comparison: Both evaluations support the evolutionary algorithm optimization results (C16-C19). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative assessment (CI = 0.877), while peer reviewers affirm the computational modeling approach more broadly. Peer review also includes C20-C21 in this evaluation, which OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

Both support the constrained model's ability to reproduce experimental observations (C23-C24). OpenEval emphasizes the necessity of inhibitory ASER-AIY connections and includes additional claims (C20-C21, C33) about synchronized activation patterns. Peer review focuses more narrowly on the comparison between constrained and unconstrained models.

Perfect agreement on klinotaxis mechanism (C25-C26). Both evaluations support the quantitative correlations between curving rate and gradient sensing. OpenEval provides specific reference to Figure 4a,c, while peer review accepts the model's ability to reproduce klinotaxis behavior without raising concerns.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about the mechanistic hypothesis (C27-C28). OpenEval identifies specific concerns about indirect EC50 inference (C44-C47) and lack of direct experimental validation. Peer review similarly notes 'key assumptions still need to be verified by biological validation,' though also includes C34-C35 which OpenEval addresses in R5.

Both support the bidirectional behavior regulation (C30). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of the ASER-AIY synaptic switching mechanism (C34-C37) with reference to Figure 5c-d. Peer review accepts the bidirectional navigation capability more generally. OpenEval notes the underlying biochemical mechanism remains hypothetical.

Partial overlap on C34-C35 regarding synaptic transition mechanism. OpenEval (R5) supports these claims as part of the encoding/decoding mechanism with simulation evidence. Peer review (R4) expresses uncertainty, noting need for biological validation of key assumptions.

Partial overlap on C36-C37 regarding synaptic plasticity role. OpenEval (R5) supports these as part of the bidirectional behavior mechanism. Peer review (R7) affirms these mechanistic insights as 'solid findings' and highlights synaptic plasticity demonstration as a key strength.

Perfect agreement on SMB inhibition results (C31-C32, C38). Both evaluations support the model's demonstration of suppressed salt preference behavior matching experimental data. OpenEval emphasizes consistency across two independent inhibition methods (Figure 6b and supplement 1b). Peer review accepts these as valid demonstrations of behavioral regulation.

Perfect agreement on cross-species comparison (C39-C40). Both evaluations support the claim of convergent evolution of phase-dependent sensorimotor coupling. OpenEval notes this is based on literature synthesis rather than new experimental data. Peer review implicitly accepts the broader relevance without raising concerns.

Partial overlap on C33 regarding synchronized ASER-AIZ activation. OpenEval (R2) includes this as evidence for the necessity of inhibitory connections. Peer review (R7) addresses this as part of broader mechanistic insights about synaptic plasticity in the circuit.

Both support the biochemical mechanism background (C41-C43). OpenEval specifically cites these as well-established findings from Hiroki et al. 2022 and Sato et al. 2021. Peer review groups these with other background claims as accepted foundation, noting the study uses 'previously described neural connections.'

Both support the C. elegans neurobiology background (C1-C5). OpenEval cites these as well-established facts providing essential context. Peer review accepts these as unquestioned foundation for the study, grouping them with extensive additional background claims.

Both support the behavioral observations background (C6-C10). OpenEval cites these as established behavioral context from literature. Peer review groups these with other background claims as accepted starting points without challenge.

Both support the klinokinesis circuit background (C11-C13). OpenEval notes these provide precedent for the proposed mechanism. Peer review accepts these as part of the established biological foundation.

Both support the AIY-AIZ inhibitory connection background (C14-C15). OpenEval emphasizes this as crucial neurophysiological constraint for the evolutionary algorithm. Peer review accepts this as part of the anatomical and physiological background.

Both support the receptor properties background (C48-C50). OpenEval notes these provide context for the proposed analogous mechanism. Peer review groups these with other background claims as accepted foundation.
Both support the food sensing pathway background (C51-C52). OpenEval cites this as biological basis for starvation effects simulation. Peer review accepts this as part of the established foundation.

Both support the minimal circuit derivation methodology (C53-C56). OpenEval validates the circuit selection approach. Peer review accepts the use of 'previously described neural connections' as valid starting point.

Both support the thermotaxis analogy background (C57). OpenEval cites this as supporting evidence for the proposed mechanism. Peer review groups this with other background claims as accepted foundation.
